transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-05-21 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Tran (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Nimbus Head of ML), Priya Shah (Nimbus Platform Eng), Carlos Mendez (CTO, joined 00:18)

Summary:
Quick product walkthrough focused on the model catalog UI and compatibility matrix. Demoed filters for task, quantization, hardware compatibility, and benchmark overlays (latency/throughput/cost per 1k tokens). Customer curious about routing between variants (fp16 vs int8 quant), on-prem options, and token-cost math. Agreed to run small benchmarks and share sample prompts.

Topics covered:
- Catalog filters and saved views
- Benchmarks overlay and sample workload comparisons
- Compatibility matrix: kernels, supported accelerators (A100/H100/T4/CPU), tokenizer/case differences
- Quantization profiles and quality tradeoffs
- Routing/fallback policies and canary deployments
- Security/priv compliance: VPC, KMS, audit logs

Transcript (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect in places):
[00:00] Sophie: hey everyone thanks for joining, hi Liam, Priya, Carlos, we're excited to show the catalog flow today and how you can pick an open model and get predictable perf and cost.
[00:12] Liam: yeah thanks, Sophie. Quick context — we run most inference on EKS today, we have a mix of A100s in prod and t4 for lower-cost batch jobs, trying to understand what models fit our realtime prompt latency and cost targets.
[00:28] Maya: perfect, that's right in line with the demo. i'll share my screen — apologies if the screen share lags.
[00:33] <screenshare starts>
[00:36] Maya: ok nav to Catalog, top-left you can filter by task (chat, generation, embeddings), model family (Llama2, Mistral-ish, openflm), and there's a quantization toggle — shows which builds support int8 / int4. note: int4 is still experimental on some vendors so we flag that.
[01:05] Priya: when you say "openflm" is that a specific distro? our naming is a bit different — sometimes tokenizer mismatch bites us.
[01:12] Maya: yeah, names get messy — our compatibility matrix includes tokenizer implementation notes, e.g., whether a model uses gpt2-style bpe vs sentencepiece; we also list max context and recommended kernel. sometimes the transcriber's gonna spell it wrong, like "open-f-l-m" in the meta but the catalog has the repo link.
[01:34] Liam: show me an example comparing a mid-sized Llama2 variant vs a Mistral-like family for 2k tokens.
[01:40] Maya: sure — i select Llama2-13B-adaptive and Mistral-7B-Instruct in the UI. on the right there's a benchmark overlay — latency p50/p95, throughput on A100/H100/T4, and an estimated cost per 1k tokens based on our pricing. you can toggle seqlen to 512/2k to see how kernels behave.
[02:05] Maya: note here the Mistral-7B has much better cost-per-token on T4 for shorter sequences, but the Llama2 13B beats it for long context when using KV-cache optimizations on H100.
[02:22] Liam: are those numbers from your public bench or from a redwood-dedicated run?
[02:26] Sophie: good question — these are mixed: the baseline bench is our standardized microbenchmark run (we link the spreadsheet), and we also show empirical numbers from dedicated instances where available. for Nimbus-specific runs we'd recommend running against your sample prompts — kernel performance varies by prompt shape.
[02:40] Priya: can we upload a sample prompt set? we'd want to see end-to-end latency including network overhead in our VPC.
[02:46] Maya: absolutely — you can upload a CSV or JSON prompt set in the Optimize tab; Optimize will run evals across selected models and hardware profiles and output a comparison matrix, with the option to store raw traces for debugging.
[03:01] Carlos (entering): sorry late — super briefly: do you support on-prem/hybrid? we have gov customers, need to know.
[03:07] Sophie: yes, Redwood Private supports VPC/on-prem deployments. we can ship a customer-controlled control plane and integrate with your KMS/HSM for key management. audit logs are available and we have SOC 2 + ISO attestation. i'll share the compliance pack after.
[03:20] Carlos: good.
[03:22] Maya: back to the demo — here's the compatibility matrix item for the Llama2-13B-adaptive:
- tokenizer: gpt2-bpe (case-sensitive)
- recommended kernel: fused-attn-v2 (H100 optimized)
- quant profiles: fp16, int8-rt (recommended for throughput), int4-experimental (quality drop flagged)
- known issues: some older tokenizers mismatch on newline tokenization (we have a normalization setting)
[03:59] Liam: when you say "quant profiles" do you also show a quality benchmark? like rouge/accuracy or ppl?
[04:06] Maya: yes, on the bench overlay you can enable "quality delta" which runs a small eval set and shows delta from fp16 baseline — it's a synthetic eval, useful for quick checks. for production you can point it at your gold prompts and metrics.
[04:20] Priya: how straightforward is switching a route to a quantized variant for cost savings? we have strict SLOs.
[04:26] Maya: in Console you can create a route and specify a tiered policy — like prefer fp16, fallback to int8 if capacity constrained, or gradual rollout to int8 with canary at 5% traffic. routing rules can be time/windowed and have automatic rollback on quality regression.
[04:40] Liam: what about tokenizer or output differences — if int8 produces slightly different completions, will you surface that?
[04:45] Sophie: yes, Optimize logs delta examples and you can set regression alerts tied to a prompt set. if the regression crosses a threshold we can auto-failover.
[04:55] Maya: showing the matrix CSV export now — it includes model id, supported hw, quant profiles, max tokens, recommended batch size for throughput, and a note column for tokenizer caveats.
[05:10] Priya: can we map this to our infra labels? we tag nodes 'prod-a100', 'batch-t4' etc.
[05:15] Maya: you can attach custom labels to hardware profiles in Dedicated/Private and then filter the compatibility matrix by label — so you'll only see entries compatible with your prod-a100 profile.
[05:25] Liam: any limitations around batch sizes and latency spikes? e.g., we need sub-150ms p95 for a 200-token average.
[05:32] Maya: two levers — batching and prefix cache. for realtime low-latency paths we recommend small batch size and prefix caching for repeated prompts; Optimize suggests an autoscaler and batching config based on target p95. the benchmark overlay shows expected p50/p95 for the chosen batch settings. and you can pin a route to a high-priority pool for lower contention.
[05:50] Carlos: curious about kernel selection — do you auto-pick kernels or is that manual?
[05:54] Maya: the runtime auto-selects kernels based on model arch, seqlen distribution, and hardware, but you can also force a kernel for diagnostics. some customers lock a kernel for determinism during compliance runs.
[06:08] Lily (transcription artifact shows "Lily" but actually Sophie): uh — will the quantized models still accept our postprocessing hooks?
[06:12] Sophie: yes hooks and function-calling are preserved; quantization is at the model weights level, not the API contract.
[06:18] Liam: about pricing math — can you walk through how you compute cost-per-1k tokens on the overlay?
[06:23] Sophie: it's a combination of measured throughput (tokens/sec) on given hardware, the effective cost of that hardware amortized to our price per-minute, plus extra charges for features like streaming, tool-calls. we show a conservative and an optimistic estimate. we'll send the calc sheet.
[06:40] Priya: any red flags for us to consider for on-prem ops? e.g., kernel compatibility with older CUDA stacks.
[06:46] Maya: yes we annotate required driver minimums; older CUDA can still work but some fused kernels need newer drivers. the compatibility matrix lists driver and libc versions per kernel.
[06:58] Liam: show me the concrete export we can run with our prompts.
[07:02] Maya: clicking Export -> Catalog CSV -> include benchmarks -> attach sample prompts. that'll give you a per-model row with the bench numbers and a link to raw traces (if you opt in).
[07:18] Sophie: for next steps we'll send the recording, the bench spreadsheet, and a short setup doc for running Optimize against a prompt set in your VPC. Maya will run the quick H100/T4 run and we'll reconvene after Nimbus uploads prompts.
[07:31] Priya: timeline wise, our procurement needs a quote; if numbers look good we'll aim to pilot in Q2.
[07:38] Sophie: understood, we'll include a rough pilot estimate in the follow-ups.
[07:44] Liam: one more question — do you support private model uploads (customer models) and then show them in the same catalog?
[07:51] Maya: yes private models appear in your catalog namespace, and the compatibility matrix will auto-populate as we run microbenchmarks. for private models you can opt out of sharing any metrics with Redwood.
[07:59] Carlos: thanks — that's important.
[08:02] Sophie: ok last bit — security, i'll drop the SOC2 pack and the KMS integration guide in the email.
[08:09] Maya: and i'll attach the bench spreadsheet and the quick-run notes.
[08:13] Liam: thanks all, this was helpful. we'll upload prompts by Friday and aim for the benchmark run next week.
[08:20] Sophie: great, thanks everyone.
[08:22] <call ends>

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels and small ASR errors (e.g., "openflm" variants, punctuation). links referenced in call: demo deck (internal link), benchmark spreadsheet (Drive link), SOC2 pack (S3 link).
